title: fix(update): place the candidate snapshot by measured capacity and exit non-zero when the update was not applied
body:
Fixes #145638
Refs #145020 #131989

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `openclaw update` exhaust a small temporary filesystem while validating an installation with large active plugin payloads. The snapshot admission counted SQLite families but omitted the plugin dependency owners that the copy worker materialized.

## Why This Change Was Made

Inventory and copying now share one file plan, including active plugin payloads and dependencies. Admission selects a usable explicit `TMPDIR`, then the existing private `<state-dir>.update-captures/` sibling, then system temporary storage, using the measured SQLite/plugin sizes and scratch budget. A typed pre-copy refusal reports the required bytes, checked destinations, available bytes, and remedy. Chosen locations and sizes survive the existing update report and wire projection.

Active payloads remain available to candidate config/startup validation. The snapshot is disposable rehearsal state; rollback continues to use its existing recovery owner. Copying uses only admitted files and bounded writes, and refuses changed owners or enlarged admitted files.

## User Impact

Updates can validate large plugin installations on machines with small `/tmp` filesystems. Operators can select a sufficiently large filesystem with `TMPDIR`, and insufficient capacity produces an actionable report before payload copying.

Release-note context: the installed 2026.9.3/2026.9.4 updater owns the first snapshot, before candidate code runs. For that first hop, use `TMPDIR=/var/tmp openclaw update --yes` on a filesystem with enough space; subsequent updates use the new allocator.

The failure/repair regression protects the existing nonzero exit when the requested update was not applied. Successful updates with warnings remain successful. No production exit-code change is claimed: current source and the tested published-driver cases already exit 1. The reporter's exit-0 observation remains an investigation gap.

## Evidence

Reporter attribution was corrected by a message-only history rewrite from `40cdb6a4c2073b21bb718d2ee9c1eb2d28b91dc1` to `c19d8f6b8c0170c5e63b8ced1b6e2261658380f3`. All three commit trees and the merge topology are identical; `git diff 40cdb6a4c2073b21bb718d2ee9c1eb2d28b91dc1 c19d8f6b8c0170c5e63b8ced1b6e2261658380f3` is empty, the branch commit count remains 3, and the branch has zero co-author trailers. `Fixes #145638` and prose reporter credit remain. The lead's scoped-clean autoreview and the ClawSweeper review of the previous head cover this identical tree; no re-review was requested. The exact-head watcher returned GREEN for [CI run 34685585888](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34685585888) on the replacement head, with zero pending checks and no rerun requested.

`node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed. Fresh P1 autoreview is scoped-clean, including the subsequent main integration and CI import-boundary repair. After integrating main, focused owner verification passed 238 tests (5 platform skips); the same 27 files passed changed-file checks. The full lane command passed all six shards before integrating concurrent main changes: 138 files / 2,799 tests passed, with 2 files / 14 tests skipped.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/update*.test.ts src/cli/update-cli packages/gateway-protocol/src/update-runs-validators.test.ts
node scripts/check-changed.mjs
```

Linux proof of the snapshot implementation used Blacksmith Testbox (`tbx_01m2a9ax43zz09k4qjc8ctfd82`, [run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34681617220)), Node 24, isolated state, and a 1 GiB tmpfs `/tmp`. The canonical package builder passed tarball integrity and import-graph checks. The later main integration retained the snapshot implementation; focused checks cover the combined warning/report paths. With a 1,200 MiB active plugin payload:

- Published 2026.9.4 failed its default snapshot with `runtime-verification-failed` and exit 1 in JSON and human modes.
- Its first hop succeeded with an explicit `TMPDIR` on the state volume.
- The fixed updater succeeded without that override, selecting `state-volume` and reporting SQLite `1,609,728`, plugin `1,258,336,256`, and required `1,333,493,760` bytes.
- On a 2 GiB state-volume cell holding the same payload, it refused before copying: required `1,333,329,920` bytes, sibling available `887,566,336`, temporary available `1,002,909,696`; typed reason `snapshot-capacity-insufficient`, exit 1.

Published 2026.9.3 was also exercised with filesystem faults on snapshot copies 1 and 3 and a real successful copy/repair oracle on 2. The installed package remained unchanged, the real repair attempt was recorded as succeeded, fresh validation failed, and the process exited 1 in JSON and human modes. Human output recorded `Repair 1: succeeded — repaired`. Its terminal ledger marks the current repairing phase failed while retaining the successful repair attempt; this is the existing terminal-record behavior, so the probe's expectation of a completed terminal repairing row was not met. No exit-0 reproduction is claimed.

Capacity regressions failed before the fix: the small temporary filesystem was selected despite the active plugin size, and the no-fit case resolved instead of refusing. Reporting regressions showed dropped capacity facts. Additional regressions reproduced unusable destination failures and unadmitted files copied after inventory; the repair now preserves the admitted copy boundary.

CI exposed a startup-bundle regression from sharing the formatter module with its runtime Zod schema. Separating the unchanged schema into its own module keeps report rendering free of that eager dependency. The existing performance gate failed at `380,057` bytes gzip before and passed at `351,579` after, against the unchanged `355,116`-byte limit. A further 136 focused tests passed after this module split. CI also found the existing top-level CLI fixture returning the retired inventory array; updating only that response shape changed its repair-order table from 11 failures / 2 passes to 13 passes, preserving all assertions.

The composed CLI test covers failed fresh snapshot → successful private repair → failed fresh snapshot → failed terminal result, unchanged installed package/launcher, and real child exit 1. Existing recovery tests cover success with warnings and exit 0.

Known limits: capacity checks cannot reserve space against unrelated concurrent filesystem writes. The snapshot remains disposable, and no new configuration, dependency, persistent schema, or protocol version is introduced.

Reported by @sootyax (#145638).


## ClawSweeper review

Reviewed the completed review for `40cdb6a4c2073b21bb718d2ee9c1eb2d28b91dc1`. No code fixups applied. The mounted-state fallback request is deferred for this scoped landing: the approved allocator uses the existing private sibling layout, which is on the parent filesystem when the state directory itself is a mount point. Such layouts may still need an explicit `TMPDIR` on a sufficiently large filesystem. Both published 2026.9.3 and 2026.9.4 used `os.tmpdir()`; the state-local fallback cited by the review was added afterward in `3acd5c945a59`. This remains a known limitation relative to that main-only fallback, including the documentation's general same-filesystem description.

The exit-0 report remains unreproduced; the published-driver and composed CLI proof above establish exit 1, so no production exit-code repair is claimed. The data-model flag concerns disposable worker inventory and optional report fields; this change introduces no SQLite schema, retention, or rollback migration. Existing published-driver upgrade proof is retained above. No re-review requested because this landing changes no code.
